theme: The Kami War: The Theft of a God and the Sisters of Flesh and Spirit
narrator_note: Kyodai herself is the once-imprisoned child/fragment of O-Kagachi, later the protector spirit bonded to Michiko. Her WUBRG activation grants a true five-color historical narrator.
canon_caveats: Kyodai is not a generic dragon and is not O-Kagachi himself; she is the freed piece/child taken from the god and bonded to Michiko.
Lord Konda causes the war by imprisoning Kyodai, though the mortal population initially believes the kami attacked without cause.
The conflict lasts roughly twenty years in the historical Kamigawa plane writeup; Neo Dynasty's framing occurs about 1,200 years later.
Toshiro helps free the captive Kyodai and is exiled by Night's Reach; label his selfishness alongside his historic contribution.
Neither Meloku nor Soratami Mirror-Mage is individually proven to have joined Konda's theft by their card printings; their cards stand for the moonfolk faction that official history describes.
The NEO Saga cards document history retrospectively. DFC back faces are not separate physical cards and are not added to the 100.

Postwar cards such as Shrine Steward, Brilliant Restoration, Spirit-Sister's Call and older ritual artifacts include thematic interpretation rather than direct evidence of a literal discrete story moment.
The NEO legendary lands are an epilogue showing Kamigawa's later geography, not claim that their modern forms existed during the original Kami War.

beats.title: I. Before the war: Konda steals a divine child

cards.name: Konda, Lord of Eiganjo
cards.why: The ruler who stole part of O-Kagachi to secure immortality, provoking the Kami War.

cards.name: Mannichi, the Fevered Dream
cards.why: The original BOK flavor records Konda's fevered vision of a spirit-child early in his reign.

cards.name: That Which Was Taken
cards.why: The imprisoned fragment of O-Kagachi, later freed as Kyodai; original BOK flavor calls it humanity's fatal captivity.

cards.name: Konda's Banner
cards.why: The daimyo's emblem and military apparatus as his authority hardens.

cards.name: Konda's Hatamoto
cards.why: One of the lord's retainers, a direct portrait of the political order shielding his crime.

cards.name: Isamaru, Hound of Konda
cards.why: The faithful hound serving Konda's court; his martial reputation survived in later Kamigawan lore.

cards.name: Masako the Humorless
cards.why: The court watcher whose original flavor establishes surveillance and loyalty under Konda.

cards.name: Kami of Ancient Law
cards.why: The original flavor invokes Konda's doctrine of order, ironically undercut by his sacrilege.

cards.name: Honden of Cleansing Fire
cards.why: A pre- and wartime shrine representing the mortal world's reverence for the white-aligned divine power.

cards.name: Honden of Seeing Winds
cards.why: One of the five original Hondens, showing the world of gods and worship before trust is broken.

cards.name: Honden of Night's Reach
cards.why: Shrine of the dark Myojin later linked to Toshiro's role in the war.

cards.name: Honden of Infinite Rage
cards.why: The red Myojin's shrine demonstrates the formidable spirits whose wrath mortals feared.

cards.name: Honden of Life's Web
cards.why: The green Myojin's shrine fills out Kamigawa's five-color prewar spiritual culture.

beats.title: II. Reito massacred: the kami turn against their worshippers

cards.name: Ghostly Prison
cards.why: Original CHK flavor memorializes Reito, destroyed in the first battles of the Kami War.

cards.name: Befoul
cards.why: Direct original narrative of the kami overwhelming and consuming the militia at Reito.

cards.name: Rend Flesh
cards.why: The original card describes the Reito massacre and the helplessness of mortal soldiers.

cards.name: Horobi, Death's Wail
cards.why: The death spirit rising from Reito's ashes, attested in the original printed flavor.

cards.name: Kami of the Waning Moon
cards.why: The original card depicts Reito's defenders scattering under renewed kami attack.

cards.name: Kabuto Moth
cards.why: The horrors of even weapon spirits attacking soldiers in the war's first days.

cards.name: Horizon Seed
cards.why: Original flavor turns peaceful shrine escorts into combat medics in the kami army.

cards.name: Night of Souls' Betrayal
cards.why: The mortal horror when kami associated with human souls themselves appear to rebel.

cards.name: Kodama of the North Tree
cards.why: Original CHK flavor says the once-slumbering kodama awakens in rage during the war.

cards.name: Kodama of the South Tree
cards.why: The friendly spirit becomes fierce during the Kami War, a printed transformation of allegiance.

cards.name: Bounteous Kirin
cards.why: The compassionate kami reluctantly join the conflict; the SOK flavor text says so outright.

cards.name: Crack the Earth
cards.why: The original BOK quote describes growing and increasingly unpredictable spirit devastation.

cards.name: Toils of Night and Day
cards.why: The original BOK flavor describes time and seasons destabilizing across Kamigawa during the war.

cards.name: Stone Rain
cards.why: The original CHK flavor describes elemental kami destruction and Eiganjo's extraordinary safety.

cards.name: Kami of the Painted Road
cards.why: Old road inscriptions of kami law become ominous war warnings in the original flavor.

beats.title: III. The mortal front: samurai, scholars, ogres and moonfolk

cards.name: Kiyomaro, First to Stand
cards.why: The Eiganjo defender celebrated by descendants for refusing to surrender the fortress.

cards.name: Opal-Eye, Konda's Yojimbo
cards.why: An actual bodyguard of Konda, representing the castle's desperate defense.

cards.name: Takeno, Samurai General
cards.why: Commander of Eiganjo's troops, named in the period's military orders and flavor.

cards.name: Kitsune Bonesetter
cards.why: A centuries-old healer turning wisdom toward casualties of the Kami War.

cards.name: Kumano, Master Yamabushi
cards.why: The mountain fighter whose yamabushi arts offered mortal resistance to spirits.

cards.name: Kumano's Pupils
cards.why: Original CHK quote recalls Kumano's pupils defeating kami before he reluctantly entered the war.

cards.name: Rend Spirit
cards.why: Mortals learn to strike against kami directly, a thematic mirror to the Reito massacre's Rend Flesh.

cards.name: Blood Rites
cards.why: Ogre rites let terrible oni escape into the mortal world, explicitly described by original flavor.

cards.name: Villainous Ogre
cards.why: Original flavor describes ogre-kind emerging from caves with demonic aid during the war.

cards.name: Heartless Hidetsugu
cards.why: The dangerous ogre mage whose oni blood-oaths and destruction become infamous.

cards.name: Hidetsugu's Second Rite
cards.why: A later original card narrating Hidetsugu's obsession with vengeance.

cards.name: Meloku the Clouded Mirror
cards.why: A major moonfolk figure; the Soratami culture is relevant to Konda's moonfolk conspiracy, but the card does not by itself prove Meloku personally performed the theft.

cards.name: Soratami Mirror-Mage
cards.why: A portrait of powerful moonfolk magic; used as factional context rather than an accusation of specific complicity.

cards.name: Field of Reality
cards.why: Original CHK quote records Minamo's scholars understanding and exploiting the veil between kami and mortals.

cards.name: Hisoka, Minamo Sensei
cards.why: Period flavor explicitly remembers Minamo surviving the Kami War through ingenuity and secrets.

cards.name: Thoughtbind
cards.why: Original quote says Azami's researchers found spells crucial to mortal survival during the war.

beats.title: IV. Toshiro and Michiko discover the truth; O-Kagachi descends

cards.name: Toshiro Umezawa
cards.why: The renegade samurai whose self-interested heroism helps free the captive spirit.

cards.name: Umezawa's Jitte
cards.why: His famous legendary blade, an unusually direct personal artifact.

cards.name: Myojin of Night's Reach
cards.why: The dark kami grants power to Toshiro, later exiling him for using it against her will.

cards.name: Choice of Damnations
cards.why: The original SOK flavor gives Toshiro's own cynical philosophy of desperate choices.

cards.name: Life of Toshiro Umezawa
cards.why: An NEO Saga that deliberately retells Toshiro's conflicted heroism, not a new 1200-year-later Toshiro.

cards.name: The Long Reach of Night
cards.why: The NEO Saga records the influence and gifts of Night's Reach on the historical events.

cards.name: Michiko Konda, Truth Seeker
cards.why: Michiko's original SOK flavor announces that she will not return until she restores her father and peace.

cards.name: Threads of Disloyalty
cards.why: Original BOK flavor documents Lord Konda's growing paranoia.

cards.name: Hero's Demise
cards.why: The original BOK text directly questions Konda's arrogance and fate in the war.

cards.name: Reverence
cards.why: Period flavor states Konda never believed he could lose despite the forces against him.

cards.name: Ribbons of the Reikai
cards.why: The original text describes the fundamental difference between mortal and spirit perception; context for crossing the worlds.

cards.name: Final Judgment
cards.why: Original BOK flavor depicts the terrified armies when O-Kagachi himself appears.

cards.name: O-Kagachi, Vengeful Kami
cards.why: The supreme original kami seeking the stolen part of himself; the C17 flavor directly names the war and stolen object.

cards.name: The Kami War
cards.why: The NEO five-color Saga is an explicit retrospective about O-Kagachi's rampage and downfall; its reverse face is O-Kagachi Made Manifest.

beats.title: V. The god is freed, Konda falls, and mortals and kami heal together

cards.name: The Fall of Lord Konda
cards.why: The original NEO saga has the broken Konda story and reverse-side Fragment of Konda flavor.

cards.name: Spirit-Sister's Call
cards.why: A thematic nod to the Kyodai–Michiko partnership; do not claim the card's rules depict a specific unverified scene.

cards.name: Michiko's Reign of Truth
cards.why: The NEO Saga's reverse-side flavor directly remembers Michiko's bond with Kyodai and the end of the war.

cards.name: Brilliant Restoration
cards.why: The original NEO flavor is a reconstruction message; included as a thematic note on healing, with the speaker not asserted.

cards.name: Era of Enlightenment
cards.why: The reverse-side NEO flavor describes laying down weapons under Kyodai's guidance.

cards.name: Reito Lantern
cards.why: An original artifact memorializing spirits and the first massacre at Reito.

cards.name: Long-Forgotten Gohei
cards.why: A prewar priestly ritual artifact, selected as a return to reverence after the conflict.

cards.name: Reki, the History of Kamigawa
cards.why: A dedicated historian preserving stories of the era; flavor explicitly describes later compilation.

cards.name: Shrine Steward
cards.why: The NEO original flavor describes transforming broken swords into peaceful shrine servants.

cards.name: Befriending the Moths
cards.why: A Saga remembering how Eiganjo's people patiently learned to train protective moths.

beats.title: VI. Land atlas: old Kamigawa and its world 1,200 years later

cards.name: Eiganjo Castle
cards.why: Konda's supposedly impregnable center of power during the Kami War.

cards.name: Minamo, School at Water's Edge
cards.why: The Minamo magicians who researched the veil between the realms.

cards.name: Shizo, Death's Storehouse
cards.why: The haunted death-land of the historical region, evoking Kamigawa's oni and spirits.

cards.name: Shinka, the Bloodsoaked Keep
cards.why: The mountain stronghold associated with ogres and the Hidetsugu era.

cards.name: Okina, Temple to the Grandfathers
cards.why: Orochi and ancestral religious culture in the old spirit world.

cards.name: Boseiju, Who Shelters All
cards.why: An original Kamigawa legendary sacred tree and spiritual landmark.

cards.name: Gods' Eye, Gate to the Reikai
cards.why: The original gate to the spirit realm, directly relevant to the breached barrier.

cards.name: Mikokoro, Center of the Sea
cards.why: A sacred historical setting used for spiritual contemplation.

cards.name: Oboro, Palace in the Clouds
cards.why: The moonfolk sky-city, a location for the Soratami culture involved in the larger conspiracy.

cards.name: Miren, the Moaning Well
cards.why: An old spiritual site representing the tormented dead of the conflict.

cards.name: Untaidake, the Cloud Keeper
cards.why: Old-Kamigawa moonfolk geography, not a claim of a specific Konda theft scene.

cards.name: Eiganjo, Seat of the Empire
cards.why: NEO era view of Eiganjo over a millennium later; historical location change, not a contemporaneous war site.

cards.name: Takenuma, Abandoned Mire
cards.why: Modern view of the marshlands that had been dangerous through the old war.

cards.name: Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance
cards.why: Modern view of the mountains where ogres and samurai fought in the war era.

cards.name: Otawara, Soaring City
cards.why: Modern view of the moonfolk's sky settlement and changing technology.

cards.name: Boseiju, Who Endures
cards.why: Modern continuation of the same revered tree, bridging 1,200 years of the plane's history.
